sb2038Check.claim: Dispatch card: SB 2038 (2023) created ETJ release by petition; if true, a derived ETJ is the fabricated buffer P-76 already refused.
sb2038Check.verdict: CONFIRMED via primary source, capitol.texas.gov/BillLookup/BillSummary.aspx?LegSess=88R&Bill=SB2038 and capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs/88R/analysis/html/SB02038F.htm -- SB 2038, 88th Texas Legislature (2023), added Local Government Code Chapter 42 Subchapters D and E, effective 2023-09-01: direct-petition and election-based ETJ release, plus automatic release by municipal inaction, plus a bar on re-inclusion absent the owner's own later request.
sb2038Check.adjacentFinding: The dispatch's own live-measured Austin data (116 of the 270 '2 MILE ETJ' rows) cites a DIFFERENT bill, SB 1844 -- independently verified as the 89th Legislature (2025), amending LGC Sec. 43.141 (disannexation for water/wastewater service failure near navigable water, eff. 2025-09-01). Per Austin's own council case records, land disannexed under SB 1844/Sec.43.141 lands IN the ETJ rather than being released from it -- consistent with those rows still carrying an ETJ label. Both bills verified real and correctly distinguished; not a data error.
sb2038Check.relevanceCarriedForward: A third real, one-off legal mechanism (Sec.43.141 disannexation) joins the AG-development-agreement carve-outs the dispatch already flagged as evidence Austin's actual ETJ is shaped by individual administrative actions, not a §42.021 population formula. This is evidence carried forward for the operator's ruling, not a ruling made here.
